description: We are ASTRIX, a six-member Mechanical Engineering team from Jyothi Engineering College, Thrissur. We are passionate about space exploration, innovation, and solving real-world challenges. We bring creativity, engineering knowledge, analytical thinking, and teamwork. We aim to develop solutions using NASA's open data. Our interests include engineering design, space technology, research, programming, data analysis, GIS, and problem-solving. We believe teamwork turns ideas into impact.
summary:
Interplanetary Survival Guide – Martian Map is a project focused on designing an integrated survival system for future human exploration of Mars. We developed a conceptual guide covering four major areas: habitat systems, survival equipment, transportation, and resource management. The proposed solutions include pressurised, insulated and dust-resistant habitats, protective suits with life-support systems, rugged rovers for exploring uneven terrain, and systems for obtaining essential resources such as power, water and oxygen from local sources.

Our project addresses the challenge of surviving in Mars' harsh environment, which includes a carbon-dioxide-rich atmosphere, extreme temperatures, low gravity and long-lasting dust storms. It is important because reliable survival systems are essential for protecting astronauts, supporting long-term missions and making future human exploration of Mars safer and more sustainable.
details: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map Our project presents an integrated conceptual survival system to support future human exploration of Mars. It focuses on four major areas: habitat systems, survival equipment, transportation and resource management. The system works by combining different engineering solutions to overcome the challenges of the Martian environment. It proposes pressurised, insulated and dust-resistant habitats to protect astronauts, protective suits with life-support systems, rugged rovers for travelling across uneven terrain, and systems to obtain essential resources such as power, water and oxygen from local sources. The main benefits are improved astronaut safety, reliable living conditions, better mobility and reduced dependence on supplies from Earth. The intended impact is to support safer and more sustainable long-term human exploration of Mars. The creative aspect of our project is the integration of four essential survival systems into one complete Martian survival guide, using a mechanical engineering approach. The main factors considered were Mars' carbon-dioxide-rich atmosphere, extreme temperatures, low gravity, long-lasting dust storms, equipment reliability and limited resupply opportunities from Earth. Tools and Technologies: The project was developed as a conceptual design and presentation. No specific coding languages, hardware prototypes or specialised software tools are documented in the current project.
